meta.name: James Quinn
meta.pageDescription: James Quinn — Staff Software Engineer specializing in high-throughput distributed systems, reliability, and data integrity at scale.
meta.heroSub: I build the systems that watch your systems. A decade at Google and Bloomberg designing distributed platforms that keep millions of queries per second honest, fast, and correct.

about.title: Reliability is a design decision, not an accident.
about.body: I'm a Staff Software Engineer with over a decade of experience at Google and Bloomberg designing, building, and scaling mission-critical, high-throughput distributed systems. My work centers on data-intensive platforms that process millions of queries per second — with a deep focus on system reliability, performance optimization, and data integrity. I lead teams that turn "it broke in production" into "we caught it before anyone noticed," and I write the C++ and Python that makes that possible at scale.

initiative.title: Teaching engineering orgs to work with AI, not around it.
paragraphs: Championed the adoption of an AI-native software development framework — the Elephant-Goldfish Model, a design-doc-first workflow validated through fresh-context AI review before a line of code is written — across multiple Google Product Areas, including parts of Search, DeepMind, and Core.

Built and delivered training spanning both the soft skills (change management, delegation, judgment) and hard skills (AI tool workflows, guardrails, design-doc practice) needed for teams to adopt the model. Delivered this training at the team, org, and company level at Google, and consulted with external client companies on AI adoption.
initiative.footnote: Under this model, my team shipped critical projects for Search and Core while doubling throughput and cutting review time in half — results that helped drive the framework's spread to additional product areas.

positions.title: Technical Lead & Manager, Feature Monitoring
bullets: Led and grew a team from 2 to 12 engineers across the US and India, fostering a culture of high performance and ownership.

Owned and scaled an internal monitoring platform analyzing the integrity of data pipelines and end-user features — expanding adoption from a single prototype (~35k QPS) to 5 major Product Areas (Search, Assistant, YouTube, Geo, Bard/Gemini) processing over 6 million QPS.
Drove an 80% improvement in alerting signal fidelity, preventing over 20 major production outages annually.
Individually contributed performance optimizations to core C++ libraries and upstream dependencies, including Google's RE2 regex engine.

positions.title: Technical Lead, Data Integrity & Search Infrastructure
bullets: Led a 5-engineer team on a C++ data integrity reporting service, verifying petabytes of data at rest across Gmail, Drive, and Photos at 1.5 million QPS.

Drove a 24x performance optimization in Google's proprietary ACL database (Zanzibar) garbage collection — cutting processing time from 24+ hours for 500 billion records to under 6 hours for 3 trillion records, saving an estimated 5 SWE-years annually.
Built a large-scale testing and diffing framework for search services handling 6 million QPS, directly informing feature development for a 15-person team.
Automated deployment of production ACL-aware search infrastructure serving 900k QPS.

Designed and built foundational log file and metric collection infrastructure in C++ and Python, handling over 10 million events/sec from a fleet of 40,000+ machines (RHEL, Ubuntu, Solaris, AIX, Windows).
The platform generated over 30,000 critical alerts daily, enabling proactive monitoring for over 10,000 internal software developers.
Managed and scaled underlying data infrastructure including Splunk, ELK, Grafana, and OpenTSDB.
Used Chef for configuration management and automation across the entire server fleet.

footer.title: Let's talk systems.
footer.body: Based in Commack, NY. Open to conversations about distributed systems, reliability engineering, and AI-native engineering practice.
